scope: Proposition 5.1 (Transfer through finite fibers) of the manuscript “A counterexample to the coarse Novikov conjecture” (preprints/A-counterexample-to-the-coarse-Novikov-conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 307 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 785e448758d66154), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let D and X be countable uniformly discrete bounded-geometry spaces. Suppose X = ` u∈D Fu is a partition into nonempty finite sets. Write ξu = |Fu|−1/2 P x∈Fu δx and let P be the orthogonal projection on ℓ2(X) onto the span of the ξu. Assume: 1. P is an operator-norm limit of finite-propagation contractions Pn on ℓ2(X); 2. for every R < ∞ there is sR < ∞ such that, whenever dD(u, v) ≤ R, there is a contraction Ouv : ℓ2(Fv) → ℓ2(Fu) of propagation at most sR with Ouvξv = ξu. For the isometry V : ℓ2 (D) ⊗ H0 −→ ℓ2 (X) ⊗ H0, V (δu ⊗ h) = ξu ⊗ h, conjugation defines a ∗-homomorphism Ad V : C∗(D) → C∗(X) between the reduced, locally compact Roe algebras.
